records.whole_original_abstract: For each fixed field of positive characteristic p, we construct a single compatible symmetric chain of Artinian ideals in two rows of variables, generated from width three. At every width n ≥ 2, its quotient has both the weak and strong Lefschetz properties exactly when p ∤ n − 1. The quadratic quotient is free over the integers, and a determinant for an arbitrary linear form gives the classification over every field extension. In particular, over the fixed infinite field 𝔽ₚ(t) both properties hold and fail at unbounded widths. This gives a negative answer to the unrestricted eventual dichotomies posed by Römer. It gives no negative answer in characteristic zero or in one row.

records.whole_original_abstract: Let V be the ordinary, uncompleted complex algebra of all finite-order finite-type invariants of links. We give a principal ideal with a nonempty actual-link zero set whose vanishing ideal strictly contains its radical. The generator is g(4g-1), where g is the sum of squared pairwise linking numbers. The obstruction is a character on the entire algebra, obtained by evaluating the standard twist-restriction polynomial at a nonintegral parameter. This gives a negative answer to the arbitrary-ideal formulation of Bar-Natan's Problem 2.27, as recorded by Ohtsuki; the separate linking-number-generated ideal question is not decided.
